neighbours.label: the imperative main verb that follows a fronted purpose, time or condition clause ('To enter, leave ...', 'When they wear out, replace ...'); the same clause followed by a subject and a finite verb stays quiet
fire: To get the discount, enter the code at checkout before midnight.
When the sauce starts to bubble, stir in the cream and the basil.
If the screen freezes, hold the power button for ten seconds.
For a crispier crust, bake the pizza on the lowest rack.
Before you leave the house, check that every window is closed.
Once the paint is dry, sand the edges lightly with fine paper.
After the race, drink plenty of water and stretch your legs.
To keep the cut flowers fresh, change the water every two days.
quiet: To get the discount, shoppers entered the code at checkout before midnight.
When the sauce started to bubble, the cook stirred in the cream and the basil.
If the screen freezes, the laptop usually restarts after ten seconds.
For a crispier crust, my aunt bakes the pizza on the lowest rack.
Before he left the house, he checked that every window was closed.
Once the paint was dry, the workers sanded the edges lightly.
After the race, the runners drank plenty of water and stretched.
To keep the cut flowers fresh, the florist changes the water every two days.
